overall: Atlanta has had a steady warming day, climbing from 80.6°F at dawn to a peak of 91.4°F by 15:00 ET, but temperatures have been completely flat from 15:00 through 17:00 with a velocity of +0.0°F/hr. At 5 PM with zero upward momentum, the diurnal heating cycle is effectively over for the day — mid-June Atlanta temperatures reliably peak between 3–4 PM and the window for additional gains is essentially closed. The high dewpoint (69.8°F) indicates a humid airmass, which can modestly cap afternoon highs.
forecast_obs_notes: Three of four models (GFS 92.2, HRRR 92.2, NBM 92.3) were tightly clustered ~0.8–0.9°F above what actually materialized, suggesting a modest warm bias in those guidance products today; ECMWF at 89.7°F undershot the observed max by 1.7°F and proved to be the outlier on the cool side. The observed running max of 91.4°F falls between the ECMWF forecast and the warm model cluster, tracking closest to a simple average of all four models (~91.6°F).
max_temp_prediction: With the temperature locked at 91.4°F since 15:00 and velocity at +0.0°F/hr at 17:00 ET, the daily maximum has almost certainly already been recorded. There is negligible probability of additional warming this late in the afternoon — any remaining upside would be a fraction of a degree at most, and the ensemble model signals (both Tier 4 Avoid with low top-bin probabilities) provide no compelling reason to expect a late surge. Confidence is high that the final TMAX will land at or extremely close to 91.4°F.
